From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: samantha@cloudfolio.com, devops@cloudfolio.com
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service stability briefing + QBR prep: April 12 Thundercache event

Team —

TL;DR: On 2026-04-12 we experienced a multi-region degradation affecting the Thundercache layer which increased tail latency and caused elevated error rates for hosted text-generation routes from 11:23–11:51 UTC. Impact summary: ~4.6% of requests experienced >500ms added latency at peak; 0.4% returned 5xx; estimated customer-facing sessions impacted ~1.2k unique API keys (top affected account: Cloudfolio). We believe a faulty cache invalidation coupled with a kernel-level regression in our inference runtime led to increased KV miss amplification.

Attached: thundercache-postmortem-draft.pdf (draft), sla-impact-chart.png (token-level SLA delta), action-register.xlsx (working tracker). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdE-example-postmortem

As part of QBR prep I need two things from leadership by Monday EOD PDT:
- Quick read/approval of the executive blurb for the customer-facing summary (two paragraphs) — see first page of the draft.
- Confirmation on SLA credit guidance for Cloudfolio (estimate in sla-impact-chart.png; need approval to proceed with credit calculation and comms).

Key timeline (short):
- 11:20 UTC: elevated error rates observed; auto-scaling masked some throughput issues.
- 11:23–11:51 UTC: root cause window; degraded KV cache hit-rate, increased round trips to origin.
- 11:51 UTC: mitigation 1 (rollback of recent kernel flag) reduced latency within 10 minutes; follow-up mitigation (cache rewarm) finished by 13:30 UTC.

Preliminary root cause: bad invalidation batch + a runtime GC/kernels regression that amplified origin load. Postmortem section 3 has experiments and evidence.

Action items I own and propose (summary):
- A1: Finalize postmortem, confirm customer statement (owner: Marissa) — due 2026-04-19 17:00 PDT.
- A2: SLA credit calc & legal sign-off (owner: Markus) — due 2026-04-20.
- A3: Hotfix plan to prevent invalidation storm (owner: Vivek -> SRE execution) — due 2026-04-25.
- A4: OKR check: add stability target to infra Q2 objectives and include metric (99.95 P99 target) (owner: Laura) — due 2026-04-22.

Please reply with approvals inline or leave comments on the draft in Drive. I will consolidate and push a customer note (soft tone, blame-free) once we have sign-off.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: thundercache-postmortem-draft.pdf, sla-impact-chart.png

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick notes inline: 

- Approve the customer blurb in the draft. Please soften references to specific kernel-level details in the public note — we can keep that for the technical postmortem.
- SLA credit: agree we should estimate. I want a conservative arithmetic approach: use token-hours impacted * average price rate + goodwill. I will coordinate legal and finance; hand off to legal by Monday morning.
- For the hotfix: SRE should create a canary rollout plan and a rollback trigger that does not depend on manual cache rewarm. Vivek, can you confirm SRE has the capacity?

Also flag for QBR: this affects our stability OKR and should be listed as a top 3 incident example for the quarter slides under "what we learned." Laura, can you slot 5 minutes in the QBR runbook to summarize mitigation and OKR catch-up?

-Markus
CTO
